rules: Search open and closed issues by marker, exact title, and semantic overlap before creating anything.
Update an existing issue when its outcome substantially overlaps; never create a duplicate merely because the title differs.
Add the idempotency marker to every created or reconciled issue body.
Assign each issue to exactly one outcome milestone.
Use dependencies as explicit body links; use GitHub sub-issues or blocked-by relationships when available.
Do not assign agents or start implementation during backlog setup.
Do not guess private GolfNow block schemas; D2 and D3 require an authoritative target package or installation.

milestones.title: M1: Verified WordPress Import
milestones.outcome: A saved fixture is converted, imported through an official WordPress path, and verified inside WordPress with zero silent loss, local media, parser-valid blocks, and a machine-readable scorecard.

milestones.title: M2: Resumable Migration Workspace
milestones.outcome: Large migrations persist incrementally, survive interruption, selectively rerun invalidated work, and export a portable versioned workspace.

milestones.title: M3: Template-Aware GolfNow Delivery
milestones.outcome: Authoritative target capabilities and versioned profiles deterministically place semantic content into real template slots and validate the resulting block tree.

milestones.title: M4: Heterogeneous Source Reliability
milestones.outcome: The generic pipeline plus bounded source adapters meets pilot fidelity thresholds across five source families and priority page types.

milestones.title: M5: Human-Replacement Pilot and Hardening
milestones.outcome: Three representative full-site shadow pilots meet the supported-envelope fidelity gates and reduce median human effort by at least 80 percent.

existing_issue_reconciliation.use_for: M1 CI gate documentation; retain and link from A1-A5
B3 bundle-wide media registry and reliable WXR URL remapping
A1 disposable WordPress import integration harness
A5 machine-readable reconciliation scorecard parent; A3 and A4 become dependencies or sub-issues
Gate 0 security/trust-boundary documentation; extend with crawler and media SSRF considerations
Only the App.tsx decomposition needed to enable safe parallel work; do not block M1 on cosmetic refactoring
Crawler test coverage supporting B1 and B2
Document QA metadata schema; link to A5 and E1

issues.title: Build a disposable WordPress import integration harness
issues.outcome: A deterministic fixture package provisions disposable WordPress, installs the official importer and required theme/plugins, imports generated delivery artifacts, and exposes the resulting state to tests.
acceptance: One documented command provisions, imports, verifies basic reachability, and tears down the fixture.
The harness has no dependency on a live source website.
Failures preserve importer logs and relevant WordPress state as CI artifacts without secrets.
Repeated runs are isolated and deterministic.

issues.title: Verify Gutenberg parsing and invalid-block absence inside imported WordPress
issues.outcome: Every imported page is parsed by WordPress and reports zero invalid or recovered blocks.
acceptance: Verifier enumerates every imported page by stable migration ID.
Report includes block names, nesting paths, parser failures, and unexpected freeform HTML.
Any invalid or recovered block fails the M1 gate.
A deliberately malformed block fixture proves failure detection.

issues.title: Reconcile imported pages, text sequence, and placeholders against saved source evidence
issues.outcome: The imported page set proves page identity, normalized text recall/order, and exact placeholder-to-exception reconciliation.
acceptance: Every expected page is matched by stable migration ID and expected slug/type/status.
Normalized meaningful text recall and order are measured per page and site.
Every placeholder ID exists once in the manifest and once in destination content unless explicitly resolved.
Missing, duplicated, or reordered content creates blocking findings.

issues.title: Reconcile imported attachment IDs, URLs, counts, and source-host references
issues.outcome: Imported pages reference the actual local WordPress attachments and no unapproved source media hosts.
acceptance: Each expected asset maps to one canonical WordPress attachment ID and URL.
Shared media is imported once and may be referenced by many pages.
Query-string and CDN source URLs reconcile by media identity rather than guessed filename.
Any unapproved source-host media URL fails the gate.

issues.title: Generate a machine-readable post-import reconciliation report
issues.outcome: One versioned JSON scorecard and human-readable HTML summary determine whether a migration passes M1.
acceptance: Report includes page, block, text, media, placeholder, link, and failure totals with stable finding IDs.
Blocking thresholds are configuration-backed and default to PRD pilot gates.
CI uploads JSON and HTML reports and fails on blocking findings.
Schema is documented and versioned for downstream QA tools.

issues.title: Define the versioned acquisition and page-snapshot contract
issues.outcome: All source acquisition stages share a validated contract for immutable response evidence and provenance.
acceptance: Schema covers requested/final URL, redirect chain, retrieval metadata, status, encoding, hashes, discovery parent, policy decision, and errors.
Original response bytes and decoded HTML are separately addressable.
Schema has semantic version and compatibility policy.
Representative success, redirect, encoding, and failure records validate.

issues.title: Archive raw response bytes, decoded HTML, metadata, and hashes during crawl
issues.outcome: Every crawl attempt produces immutable, content-addressed source evidence that supports reprocessing without recrawling.
acceptance: Successful HTML pages store raw bytes, decoded HTML, acquisition record, and matching hashes.
Redirects, non-HTML responses, and failures still create attempt records.
Re-running acquisition does not overwrite prior immutable evidence.
A conversion run can consume archived HTML with network access disabled.

issues.title: Build a bundle-wide media registry and reliable WXR URL remapping
issues.outcome: A bundle-wide registry deduplicates media by acquired content identity, tracks every source reference, and maps it to actual destination attachment identity.
acceptance: Registry records all observed URLs, content hash, MIME, dimensions, provenance, uses, and import state.
One acquired asset shared across pages produces one attachment item.
Destination URLs are reconciled from WordPress rather than guessed.
Failures retain source references and produce placeholders or blocking findings according to policy.

issues.title: Support lazy-loaded, CDN, picture, and srcset media acquisition
issues.outcome: The media discovery layer accounts for modern and legacy source URL patterns without losing responsive or lazy-loaded images.
acceptance: Supports src, srcset, picture/source, common lazy attributes, relative/protocol-relative URLs, and query strings.
Selection policy records all candidates and the chosen acquisition URL.
MIME and file content are validated independently of extension.
Missing or unsafe candidates produce explicit findings.

issues.title: Export a portable raw-HTML and source-evidence package
issues.outcome: Operators can export and inspect the saved source, and future conversion/QA runs can use it without the live site.
acceptance: Export includes original HTML, acquisition JSON, hashes, URL index, and errors for all attempted pages.
Paths are stable and safe for duplicate filenames/URLs.
Export excludes credentials and sensitive request headers.
An import/offline test reconstructs page snapshots from the package.

issues.title: Define semantic IR v1, validation, and schema-migration policy
issues.outcome: A typed, source-agnostic semantic document becomes the stable boundary between extraction and target compilation.
acceptance: IR includes all minimum PRD node types and ordered children.
Every node retains stable ID, source evidence reference, confidence/method, and asset references.
Unknown content is representable without loss.
Schema versioning and backward compatibility are documented and tested.

issues.title: Emit semantic IR from the current extraction and tokenization pipeline
issues.outcome: The existing source pipeline emits valid IR while preserving content order, assets, and audit evidence.
acceptance: Current supported elements map to the correct IR nodes.
All asset tokens become asset IDs with no token drift.
Boilerplate exclusions are explicit audit events.
Golden fixtures prove no regression in current text/image accountability.

issues.title: Compile core text, list, quote, code, and table IR nodes to Gutenberg blocks
issues.outcome: Supported textual IR nodes compile deterministically to editable native Gutenberg blocks.
acceptance: Nested lists, headings, inline marks/links, quotes, code, and tables preserve supported semantics.
Identical IR and compiler version produce byte-stable block output.
Each source node records the destination block path.
Unsupported attributes create findings rather than raw HTML fallback.

issues.title: Compile image and gallery IR nodes using reconciled media identity
issues.outcome: Images and ordered collections become native image/gallery blocks tied to media-registry identities and later destination attachments.
acceptance: Image blocks preserve alt, caption, credit/link policy, and source node mapping.
Gallery item count and order are deterministic.
Serializer supports a pre-import provisional identity and post-import actual attachment rewrite.
Unresolved media produces an explicit placeholder/finding.

issues.title: Compile embeds and unknown IR nodes to safe HTML or migration placeholders
issues.outcome: Approved embeds are sanitized and audited; everything else survives as a visible, manifest-backed exception.
acceptance: Allowlist controls hosts, protocols, tags, and attributes.
Scripts and inline event handlers never pass through.
Every placeholder contains a safe stable exception ID and remediation summary.
Full original HTML remains only in source evidence, not the placeholder block.

issues.title: Add WordPress parser round-trip and deterministic compiler tests
issues.outcome: Every compiler fixture parses with the WordPress-compatible parser and remains semantically stable across serialize/parse cycles.
acceptance: All generated fixtures parse without recovery or invalid blocks.
Block names, attributes, nesting, and inner content match expected normalized trees.
Output is deterministic for identical inputs.
Malformed and unsafe fixtures fail clearly.

issues.title: Define target-capability snapshot and template-profile v1 contracts
issues.outcome: A versioned contract describes actual target blocks, templates, patterns, slots, constraints, defaults, and capability fingerprints.
acceptance: Schemas cover all PRD-required capability and profile fields.
Slots express allowed nodes/blocks, cardinality, order, nesting, required state, and fallback.
Profile version and target fingerprint are mandatory.
Examples use authoritative data or clearly labeled synthetic fixtures.

issues.title: Build a WordPress target introspector for blocks, patterns, templates, and theme.json
issues.outcome: An authenticated WordPress-side tool exports a validated capability snapshot from the designated target installation.
acceptance: Exports WordPress/theme/plugin versions, registered blocks/schemas, patterns, templates, template parts, and relevant theme.json settings.
Snapshot validates against D1 and includes a reproducible fingerprint.
Secrets and user content are excluded.
Tool fails with actionable diagnostics when required plugins/capabilities are missing.

issues.title: Build the template-profile validator and seed-pattern slot annotation format
issues.outcome: Architects can author a profile from an authoritative seed block tree and receive deterministic validation errors for slots and constraints.
acceptance: Validator checks target fingerprint, block availability, slot uniqueness, cardinality, defaults, and fallback rules.
Slot annotations do not create invalid Gutenberg markup.
Unknown blocks or attributes fail before conversion.
Profile examples document locked and operator-editable regions.

issues.title: Build deterministic page classification and placement-plan generation
issues.outcome: Semantic pages are classified and assigned to named profile slots before serialization, with explicit confidence and unplaced-node findings.
acceptance: Planner output lists every source node exactly once as placed, intentionally ignored, or excepted.
Required slots and constraint violations block compilation.
Rules are deterministic; any model-assisted suggestion is recorded and validated.
Low confidence produces a QA finding rather than a silent generic-slot fallback.

issues.title: Compile placement plans into seeded target Gutenberg block trees
issues.outcome: Template selection materially and deterministically changes the destination block tree by filling approved seed slots.
acceptance: Seed blocks outside editable slots remain intact.
Placed nodes appear only in their assigned slots and preserve order.
Defaults and profile styles come from the profile rather than source HTML.
Compilation rejects mismatched target fingerprints or unsatisfied blocking constraints.

issues.title: Add template-conformance QA and two authoritative profile fixtures
issues.outcome: The imported result proves slot, block, and constraint conformance for two materially different real target profiles.
acceptance: Same IR compiles and imports successfully into two distinct profile structures.
Verifier checks required slots, allowed blocks, nesting, cardinality, and target fingerprint.
Profile changes invalidate only dependent planning/compilation stages.
Missing authoritative target data blocks this issue explicitly rather than being guessed.

issues.title: Define the migration-workspace manifest and stage dependency graph
issues.outcome: One versioned manifest connects source, assets, semantic documents, profiles, conversions, delivery, and QA with dependency hashes.
acceptance: Manifest covers all required logical entities and producer/input versions.
Stage invalidation rules are explicit and deterministic.
Stable IDs survive export/import and reruns.
Backward-compatibility policy and corrupt-manifest behavior are documented.

issues.title: Implement a filesystem, SQLite, and content-addressed workspace store
issues.outcome: Production-sized local jobs persist manifests and indexes in SQLite while immutable source/media blobs are stored by content hash.
acceptance: Writes are atomic and recoverable after process interruption.
Blobs are deduplicated by hash and verified on read.
Indexes query pages/assets/findings without loading the entire workspace.
Store does not depend on browser localStorage.

issues.title: Add incremental checkpoints, pause/resume, and crash recovery
issues.outcome: A large batch resumes safely from the last committed stage after normal pause or forced process termination.
acceptance: Pause stops at a safe boundary and records resumable state.
Forced interruption during a 100-page fixture run resumes without duplicate pages/assets/delivery.
In-progress records are distinguished from committed results.
Recovery emits an audit event and integrity result.

issues.title: Add selective retry and dependency-based invalidation
issues.outcome: Operators can retry failed/warned pages or rerun only stages invalidated by input, profile, or implementation changes.
acceptance: Changing a template profile reruns planning/compile/QA but not acquisition.
Changing source evidence invalidates downstream stages for only affected pages/assets.
Retry selection is recorded in the audit log.
Successful unaffected work is neither recomputed nor duplicated.

issues.title: Add portable workspace export/import and compatibility tests
issues.outcome: A complete migration workspace can move between machines, reopen without the live source, and survive supported schema upgrades.
acceptance: Export includes all PRD-required config, evidence, media, IR, plans, output, delivery, QA, and redacted logs.
Import verifies hashes and rejects unsafe paths or corrupt archives.
Offline reprocessing succeeds from the imported workspace.
At least one prior schema fixture upgrades successfully.

issues.title: Build a site-wide canonical URL and redirect map
issues.outcome: Every discovered internal URL has a stable classification and intended destination or explicit unresolved state before final delivery.
acceptance: Map covers requested, canonical, redirected, fragment, download, mailto, tel, external, and malformed URLs.
Normalization preserves distinctions that affect destination identity.
Redirect export is deterministic.
Conflicts and cycles create findings.

issues.title: Rewrite and verify internal links and anchors after delivery
issues.outcome: Internal links resolve to actual destination permalinks and valid anchors, while intentional external links remain unchanged.
acceptance: Rewrite uses destination records rather than guessed slug conventions.
Fragments are preserved only when the target anchor exists; missing anchors are findings.
Post-import verifier reports broken/unresolved internal links by page and source node.
External/mailto/tel/download policies are test-covered.

issues.title: Define and implement the migration-exception lifecycle
issues.outcome: Unsupported, unsafe, or unresolved elements become durable work items with visible placeholders and auditable resolution state.
acceptance: Exception includes all PRD-required identity, evidence, severity, remediation, ownership, and resolution fields.
Placeholder-to-exception relationship is one-to-one until explicit resolution.
Resolving an exception records who/when/how and destination artifact.
Unresolved blocking exceptions prevent release approval.

issues.title: Build migration risk scoring and QA queue filters
issues.outcome: QA operators see blocking and high-risk pages first and can filter by the dimensions defined in the PRD.
acceptance: Risk score is deterministic and explains contributing findings.
Filters cover severity/status, page type/profile, confidence, exception/media/link class, changed state, and review state.
Queue supports stable sorting and deep links to page evidence.
No raw customer content is sent to product telemetry.

issues.title: Add the page evidence view and targeted stage-rerun controls
issues.outcome: An operator can inspect saved source, semantic/placement evidence, destination result, and findings, then rerun only the affected work.
acceptance: View exposes safe source evidence, IR/plan, block mapping, destination preview/reference, findings, and exception state.
Rerun controls show which stages will invalidate before confirmation.
Controls cannot recrawl or publish without explicit authorization.
Changed results retain prior audit history.

issues.title: Define the bounded source-adapter interface and CMS-detection evidence
issues.outcome: Source-specific logic can improve detection/extraction while emitting the canonical IR and never owning Gutenberg serialization.
acceptance: Interface covers detection evidence, content-root/boilerplate suggestions, media expansion, structured page hints, confidence, and diagnostics.
Generic extraction remains the fallback.
Adapters cannot emit Gutenberg blocks or bypass IR validation.
Conflicting adapter detections resolve deterministically and visibly.

issues.title: Add a WordPress source adapter and representative fixtures
issues.outcome: Classic and Gutenberg WordPress sources gain higher-confidence content-root, media, and page-type extraction without pipeline forks.
acceptance: Detects WordPress with recorded evidence and bounded confidence.
Handles classic content, serialized block markup, captions, galleries, and common lazy media.
Output validates as canonical IR.
Fallback generic extraction remains equivalent or better when detection is uncertain.

issues.title: Add Drupal and Joomla source adapters with representative fixtures
issues.outcome: Drupal and Joomla sources gain bounded detection and extraction improvements through the common adapter contract.
acceptance: Each adapter records detection signals and confidence.
Common content containers, images, captions, and structured page hints emit valid IR.
CMS chrome/boilerplate exclusions are audited.
Generic fallback and adapter output are compared in golden tests.

issues.title: Add hosted-builder and malformed legacy-static reliability fixtures
issues.outcome: The generic pipeline is measured against builder-style markup and malformed legacy HTML without pretending to support proprietary behavior.
acceptance: Corpus covers hosted-builder-style wrappers, static tables/layout markup, invalid nesting, encoding problems, and repeated chrome.
Every expected content/asset disposition is asserted.
Proprietary interactions become exceptions, not copied scripts.
Any generic heuristic change is regression-tested across all source families.

issues.title: Detect and preserve gallery and slideshow semantic collections
issues.outcome: Ordered slideshow/gallery assets, captions, links, and behavior requirements survive source-specific markup as one semantic collection.
acceptance: Detector preserves item count, order, captions, links, and source evidence.
Duplicate thumbnail/full-size references resolve to intended asset identity.
Interactive behavior requirements are recorded separately from static media.
Unsupported behavior produces a manual-rebuild exception adjacent to an allowed static gallery when policy permits.

issues.title: Create the cross-CMS corpus scorecard and supported-envelope report
issues.outcome: Every release shows measured fidelity by source family, page type, template profile, and failure class, and explicitly states the supported envelope.
acceptance: Scorecard reports all PRD pilot metrics overall and by cohort.
Regression thresholds fail CI/release promotion.
Unsupported or underperforming cohorts are explicitly excluded with evidence.
Report links each failure class to fixtures and open issues.

issues.title: Prepare representative pilot cohorts and human-team baselines
issues.outcome: The M5 pilots have approved site cohorts, privacy boundaries, target profiles, and comparable human effort/defect baselines.
acceptance: At least three cohorts represent priority source/page/template combinations.
Baseline captures pages/day, active QA/remediation minutes, defects, and exception classes.
Raw-content retention and access rules are approved before capture.
Success and abort criteria are written before pilot execution.

issues.title: Define the supported production envelope and pilot go/no-go scorecard
issues.outcome: Product and architecture approve the exact conditions under which Blockify may be called a human-team replacement.
acceptance: Envelope names supported source families, page types, profiles, content classes, scale, privacy mode, and known exclusions.
Scorecard includes every human-replacement gate from the PRD.
Severity definitions and publication authority are assigned.
Any exception to a gate requires an explicit dated decision and owner.

issues.title: Run three full-site shadow migrations and measure interventions, time, and defects
issues.outcome: Three representative migrations run alongside or against a human-team baseline and generate comparable, auditable evidence.
acceptance: Each pilot uses saved source evidence and an approved target profile.
Every manual intervention records category, active minutes, reason, and result.
Escaped defects are independently reviewed and severity-rated.
Pilot results are reproducible from the retained/redacted workspace according to policy.

issues.title: Build operator runbooks, recovery controls, and privacy-retention procedures
issues.outcome: Operators can start, pause, recover, diagnose, export, retain, and delete migrations safely without developer intervention.
acceptance: Runbooks cover normal operation, failed import, corrupt workspace, provider outage, partial media failure, and rollback/escalation.
Retention/deletion/export procedures identify authority and evidence handling.
Diagnostic bundles exclude secrets and obey privacy policy.
A non-developer operator completes a tabletop recovery exercise.

issues.title: Close dominant pilot failure classes and rerun the full corpus
issues.outcome: All blocking pilot failure classes are represented by fixtures, fixed through child issues, and shown not to regress other cohorts.
acceptance: Each blocking failure gets a minimal legal fixture and linked child bug.
Fixes include unit/contract/integration coverage proportional to risk.
Full corpus meets approved pilot thresholds after fixes.
Remaining exclusions are documented in the supported envelope.

issues.title: Produce release-candidate evidence and the human-replacement readiness decision
issues.outcome: Decision-makers receive one evidence package supporting a clear go, conditional-go, or no-go designation and truthful product positioning.
acceptance: Package includes versioned corpus and pilot scorecards, supported envelope, open risks, security/privacy sign-off, and operator readiness.
Every PRD human-replacement gate has a measured value and pass/fail disposition.
Conditional exceptions have owners and dates.
Product wording matches the decision: accelerator until all mandatory gates pass.
